summary: Sheet Harbour Passage range lights: two wooden towers built in 1915 to lead ships into the passage; kept by the Wambolt family, then caretakers. Current status disputed.

access.note: Grounds open and towers closed (Lighthouse Friends; Rowlett). Canadian Coast Guard property.

notes_for_editor: Moderate-to-thin station. Most dated facts come from one Lighthouse Friends pair, which cites the annual reports 'various years' and E. H. Rip Irwin, Lighthouses & Lights of Nova Scotia (2003); neither was read here. STATUS IS UNRESOLVED: OpenStreetMap (the record's source) says active; Rowlett says inactive since 2024; the Coast Guard Atlantic list (Fs151-9-2025-12) has the Sheet Harbour Passage light and bell buoy XP7 but no range-tower entries. A human should check with the Coast Guard. MATCHED BY POSITION in OCR tables: (a) James Wambolt's 'May 11, 1887 .. 70 00' line, 1910v44i11p21_0659 scan 170 (printed 162): the name is unique to this station in the corpus; the page image confirms the Sheet Harbour Passage row; the salary there ($70) conflicts with Lighthouse Friends' $50 for 1887; (b) 'G. W. Wambolt (temp.)' in 1916v51i17p21_1196 scan 80 (printed 72); the page image confirms the Sheet Harbour passage row (appointed Dec. 25 1911, salary $115). Fact-checker, 2026-10-28, viewed the page images: the four annual-report footnotes had the wrong scan numbers and are corrected (works table scan 53, printed 45; G. W. Wambolt scan 80, printed 72; bell buoy scan 79, printed 71; James Wambolt scan 170, printed 162). The works table's contractor 'A. Balcon, Halifax' and the 'Inspection, etc.' line ($303.75) are visible in the image but are not in the OCR text, so the quote check cannot verify them. Rowlett's entries for both towers carry 'Inactive since 2024' and the stripe; the Coast Guard December 2025 list has one Sheet Harbour Passage entry (light and bell buoy XP7, no. 597) and no range-tower entry. The works line 'Erection of wrooden range light' (scan 53, 1917v52i13p21_1280, printed 45) is OCR'd with 'wrooden'; quote kept as printed. The Department line is a single 'wooden range light' at $1,792; Lighthouse Friends says 'twin towers' for the same sum. Lighthouse Friends' front coordinates (44.858333, -62.448889) differ from the record's OSM position (-62.448246), about 50 m; not proposed as a correction. Wrecks: a grep of Sheet Harbour in the 1900-1924 reports found no wreck tied to the range lights; one 1910 stranding 'near Sheet harbour' has an unreadable vessel name and is not tied to the range, so it is left out. Caretaker's daughter anecdote is Lighthouse Friends' report of a family recollection, attributed in the text.
